note: This event is visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2025-04-01T17:53Z. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk at the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location. Additionally, due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available to confirm the measured parameters.

note: Narrow, jet-like CME seen accelerating to the northeast primarily in SOHO LASCO C2 and also farther to the north in STEREO A COR2; the CME is with low confidence associated with a minor eruption with northern deflection from the northeastern side of Active Region 14046 (N10E10) seen starting around 2025-04-02T08:44Z in GOES SUVI 284 imagery, but triangulation suggests that the eruption originates from the far-side, and indeed, moving field lines are seen off the northeast limb primarily in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft leading edge measurement using triangulation to determine the longitude of the source; the CME becomes very diffuse with time and is extremely difficult to see in STA COR2 past 8 solar radii.

note: Faint loop CME seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, SE in STEREO A COR2. Source is an eruption seen starting at 2025-04-03T03:24Z from AR 4045 (S15W05) with Eastern deflection. Brightening and ejecta seen deflected to the east as seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2025-04-03T03:24Z. SDO AIA imagery was in a data gap which lasted from 2025-04-02T15:52Z to 2025-04-03T04:54Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement of faint leading edge using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and STEREO A COR2. Strong eastern and southern deflection was visible from the source location seen in UV imagery of the Earth-facing disk, which is reflected in the best fit parameters.

note: Faint loop CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and NE in STEREO A COR2. Source is slight dimming seen at 2025-04-03T06:48Z in SDO AIA 193 from N20W15.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and two frames of STEREO A COR2.

note: This CME is visible to the E/SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap beginning at 2025-04-03T15:23Z. The source is a filament eruption visible along the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 near S25E70 starting around 2025-03-04T17:32Z. Additionally moving/opening field lines are visible in GOES SUVI 171, 195, and 284, as well as brightening which is best seen in GOES SUVI 195. There is a data gap in SDO/AIA during the eruption for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO imagery and possible source location longitude.

note: CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source is a filament eruption from sightly over the east limb ~N15, observed as filament ejecta and field line movement starting around 2025-04-04T02:48Z in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A.

note: Very narrow CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, which becomes diffuse halfway through the STEREO A COR2 field of view. The precise source is unclear, but several small instances of field line movement on can be seen just beyond the SW limb occurring between 2025-04-04T05:00Z-07:00Z in STEREO A EUVI 195 from a bright cluster of formerly numbered ARs, including ARs 4047, 4040, and 4042, which together span from about latitude S00 to S20 and longitude W90 to W110.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using best fit between several SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 frames. The leading edge becomes diffuse halfway through the STEREO A COR2 field of view.

note: Faint front seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only due to a STEREO COR2A data gap beginning  at 2025-04-04T10:38Z, better seen in SOHO LASCO running difference imagery than white light. No source for this CME is observed in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only due to the data gap in STEREO COR2A and no observed source.

note: Faint CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and directly S in STEREO COR2A. The source is likely dimming in the far southern area of the disk, centered around S60W20, observed in SDO AIA 193 around 2025-04-04T15:00Z. This may, unlikely, be related to a C4.4 flare from AR 14502 (S23W29) which peaked at 2025-04-04T14:46Z, it is difficult to discern if this flare erupted in this deflected direction, the dimming at S60W20 is an sympathetic eruption, or if the dimming at S60W20 is entirely separate. Thus it is not currently attributed as a source, and noted for completion of the analysis.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A, tracking well with the far southern latitude dimming around S60W20 observed in SDO AIA 193.

note: CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. Source is a filament eruption from just beyond the NW limb. A prominence from just beyond the limb can be seen beginning to liftoff starting at 2025-04-04T16:08Z in GOES SUVI 304. Opening field lines seen in GOES SUVI 284 and ejecta seen in GOES SUVI 304 both show strong northern deflection of this eruption, with ejecta traveling nearly due north. STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304 show that the prominence was centered at about N30 and spanned from W82-W92 (in SDO coordinates).

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement of leading edge using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Strong northern deflection was visible from the source location seen in UV imagery from SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI, and GOES SUVI, which is reflected in the best fit parameters.

note: Faint outflow-like CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. Source is narrow ejecta and brightening seen at N20W97 (SDO AIA coordinates) in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2025-04-04T17:45Z. This small eruption may have possibly disrupted surrounding coronal material, resulting in the faint, wide, and slow leading edge which surrounds the narrow flux rope visible in SOHO LASCO C2. This CME overlaps to the south of the preceding CME:2025-04-04T16:36Z. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-04T17:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the faint leading edge, based on source location seen in STEREO A EUVI and fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-04T17:38Z. The leading edge becomes diffuse only a handful of frames into the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: Faint CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. No clear source of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is some uncertainty due to lack of clear source in available EUV imagery.

note: A bright symmetrical partial halo seen to the east in both coronagraphs. Its source is a clear, wide opening of field lines behind the east limb seen ~2025-04-05T03:55Z in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284, later followed by post-eruptive arcades gradually appearing from behind the east limb, as seen in SDO AIA 193/304/131. It overlaps with a slightly later CME that is seen as a more full halo in STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very approximate analysis of the main brightest front/loop, obtained by fitting with two coronagraphs. Based on the coronal signatures, the source is behind the east limb, but close enough to the limb for the tops of the post-eruptive arcades to start peaking from behind the limb two hours after the eruption.

note: A partial halo CME to the northeast, significantly overlapping with the 2025-04-05T04:00Z CME, and more clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery, in which its front is seen as a separate northeastern halo-like front, following the more eastern front of the earlier 2025-04-05T04:00Z CME. In SOHO its front is harder to trace because of the overlap of two CMEs. Its source is likely far behind the east limb and might be indicated by the large filament behind the northeast limb moving northward, as seen in AIA SDO 304 and GOES SUVI 304 and 284 imagery after 2025-04-05T05:00Z, although this filament is more likely to be the source of a later, more northern, 2025-04-05T09:48Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: A very approximate, speculative analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The source is likely far behind the east limb and the front is not clear as the CME is largely overlapping with the earlier CME.

note: Faint northward CME with messy multiple fronts, overlapping with 2025-04-05T04:00Z and 2025-04-05T06:36Z CMEs (this overlap makes analysis difficult). The start of the CME is likely significantly earlier, around 2025-04-05T08:36Z, but its front in the early timestamps is very difficult to discern because of the overlap. The source could be the large filament behind the northeast limb moving northward, as seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 after 2025-04-05T05:00Z, but it is unclear whether this filament is the source of this CME - or the 2025-04-05T06:36Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based solely on the fit with two coronagraphs, since the source is not completely clear and is likely behind the limb.

note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided, as an opening of field lines is observed over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2025-04-06T03:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: This CME is visible to the north/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an opening of field lines visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2025-04-06T06:30Z. Around this time there is a minor eruption observed near Active Region 14050 (N28W45) which may be associated with this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: Faint and narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. There is no clear source apart from some subtle and slow field line movement visible on the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 around 2025-04-06T16:15Z. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which lasted from 2025-04-06T10:53Z to 2025-04-06T17:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-Sky measurement in swpc_cat taken using multiple frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 running difference imagery. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which lasted from 2025-04-06T10:53Z to 2025-04-06T17:23Z.

note: Narrow CME with a faint loop-like leading edge visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, and a few frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The leading edge becomes diffuse partway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

note: Faint and narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. There is no clear source for this eruption, however, due to its similarity to earlier eruptive activity, it is possible that the source is associated with the ongoing minor field line movement and minor eruptive activity from beyond the E/NE limb. The leading edge becomes diffuse early in the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-06T20:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-Sky measurement in swpc_cat taken using multiple frames of SOHO LASCO C2 running difference imagery. The leading edge becomes diffuse early in the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view. There was no STEREO A COR2 imagery available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-06T20:53Z.

note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures visible on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

note: CME to the northeast with the source and eruption observed slightly beyond the northeast limb starting around 2025-04-07T12:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The source is behind the northeast limb.

note: Faint CME to the east in coronagraphs, following and overlapping with 2025-04-07T14:00Z CME. It is more clearly seen in running difference imagery than in the white light imagery. The source could be a very minor eruption/post eruptive arcade seen on/behind the east limb in SDO AIA 131/193 at 2025-04-07T14:12Z

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. The source marked by post eruptive arcades seems to be just beyond the east limb.

note: Fast loop CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the east-southeast in STEREO A COR2, quickly leaving the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view and comprised of a faint, asymmetric shock seen to the northeast. The likely source is an eruption seen near the vicinity of Active Region 4057 near N10E55 to E65 (after deflection), characterized by a brightening near the footpoints and a subsequent ejection of magnetic field flux seen occurring to the east starting around 2025-04-08T05:45Z, best in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 304. The eruption is also seen, though not as strongly in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284. Also associated with a type II radio burst with begin time 05:53Z and velocity 456 km/s.

cmeAnalyses.note: Two spacecraft bulk measurement with high confidence in parameters, good fit relative to observed source location.
Shock measurement in SOHO and STEREO A by encompassing the faint northeast edge in both spacecraft as well as the bright bulk.

note: Narrow CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the east-southeast in STEREO A COR2, quickly leaving the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view. The likely source is a secondary eruption seen near the vicinity of Active Region 4057 near N10E55 to E65 (after deflection) following CME: 2025-04-08T06:00Z characterized by a brightening near the footpoints and a subsequent ejection of plasma seen occurring to the east starting around 2025-04-08T08:00Z, best in SDO AIA 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using two spacecraft to triangulate the longitude out to 14 solar radii.

note: A super faint minor CME/outflow to the southwest, with mostly the left boundary seen in the coronagraph. It is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and in a few early timestamps of C3 because of its faintness and is not discernible in STEREO A COR2. Surprisingly, a clear source for this minor event can be clearly seen on/behind the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 starting after 2025-04-08T06:42Z - a field line moving very slowly, over several hours, in southwestern direction.

cmeAnalyses.note: The CME is only seen in SOHO LASCO coronagraph and is not seen in STEREO A coronagraph (likely because of its faintness). The source is on or behind the southwest limb, so it is not clear what the longitude of this event is. Only plane-of-sky measurement is possible.

note: Minor CME seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 which appears to be associated with an eruption from the eastern limb seen as open field lines starting around 2025-04-08T14:50Z best in SDO AIA 171, 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated parameters based on best fit with more imagery.
Preliminary measurement using few frames in both SOHO and STEREO A that don't overlap as the CME continues to propagate outwards to 6 solar radii.

note: This CME is visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. It is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap beginning around 2025-04-08T18:00Z. The source appears to be beyond the NE limb based on moving/opening field lines visible starting around 2025-04-08T20:12Z in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on a plane-of-sky fit using the swpc_cat measurement technique and best fit of CME features.

note: Faint CME with the fuzzy front to the NNE in both coronagraphs, with the front so faint that it is clearly seen in C3 only in a couple of early timestamps and too faint/fuzzy to discern in later timestamps. | Source is a mid-sized filament eruption centered around N26E38, as seen in SDO AIA 304/193, GOES SUVI 304/284 and (close to the NE limb) in EUVI A 304/195 starting ~2025-04-09T05:06Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the location of the source (filament eruption on disk) and confirmed by the fit in two coronagraphs. The longitude can vary a bit (+-5 degrees).

note: A very faint narrow but fast jet to the northeast in both coronagraphs. Its source could be a narrow filament eruption off the northeast limb seen in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 at ~2025-04-09T06:39Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the approximate location of the likely source - filament off the northeast limb. The jet is seen only in a few timestamps of SOHO and STEREO because of its faintness, so this analysis is very approximate.

note: Faint and narrow jet CME visible to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z. There was no clear source for this CME; there are several small instances of field line movement in the Western hemisphere of the disk and on the West limb, but none distinct enough to consider as a candidate source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement of the faint leading edge using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and two frames of SOHO LASCO C3. Unable to be tracked farther than two frames in SOHO LASCO C3, due to the C3 running difference imagery being heavily affected and/or corrupt beginning at timestamp 2025-04-09T22:40Z. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

note: Faint CME seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2. Leading edge begins to become diffuse about halfway through the SOHO LASCO C2 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z. Source is opening field lines on the E limb spanning from N00 to N05 and located between possibly E80 to E90, or slightly further beyond the limb, as seen starting as early as 2025-04-09T22:18Z in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and using only C2 frames, since this CME has not yet reached the C3 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

note: Faint and narrow CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2; this CME becomes diffuse before leaving the C2 field of view. Source is uncertain, but may possibly be a very faint instance of field line opening seen around 2025-04-09T22:27Z in SDO AIA 171 on the SW limb at S30 with strong southern deflection. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement taken using only C2 frames. Leading edge becomes diffuse before leaving C2 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-09T18:53Z.

note: Faint CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A. The source is some filament ejecta from AR 14048 (S16W71) observed in SDO AIA 304 at 2025-04-10T08:12Z, along with field line movement in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement with SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A imagery. LASCO C2 is not used due to the faintness of the front, it is better resolved in C3 and COR2A.

note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 at 2025-04-10T15:24Z. Also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely some field line movement visible beyond the NE limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2025-04-10T14:49Z and in SDO AIA 171 starting at  2025-04-10T14:36Z. The CME is also seen lifting off from behind the NE limb in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2025-04-10T14:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow (<10 degree half-width), jet-like CME first seen to the WSW in SOHO LASCO C2. Also seen to the WSW is SOHO LASCO C3 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2. The source of this jet-like CME is most likely a small but bright eruption in the vicinity of Active Region 14048 starting around 2025-04-10T16:39Z in SDO AIA 304. This eruption can also be seen as a brightening in the vicinity of Active Region 14048 in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of triangulation and ambiguity of source location near the W limb. Measurement made with running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 using SWPC_CAT.

note: Extremely faint and narrow CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2. The leading edge becomes diffuse before leaving the C2 field of view. Source is unclear, but there is continual flickering and field line movement from AR 4055 (N08W43), including a small instance of southward directed field line movement seen starting at 2025-04-11T12:45Z in SDO AIA 171. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the faint leading edge using four frames of SOHO LASCO C2. Measurement was made using the candidate source longitude, taking into consideration the heavy southern deflection which was possibly indicated in UV imagery. The leading edge becomes diffuse before leaving the C2 field of view. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: Faint and wide loop CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2. Source is field line movement and gradual dimming seen from AR 4058 (N18W50) and AR 4055 (N08W45), as well as field line movement seen on the NW limb, starting at 2025-04-11T16:33Z in SDO AIA 171. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit using several frames of C2 and a few frames of C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: Wide loop CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2. Source is an eruption near the NE limb, seen as a rising loop of opening field lines starting at 2025-04-11T20:40Z in SDO AIA 171. There are two connected rising loops seen on the E limb, which lift off together in the same eruption. One spans from approx. N22 to N30 along E70, while the other spans from approx. N35 to N50 along E90. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location and best fit in several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2. Source is opening field lines seen on the SW limb, at S35W90, with some southern deflection in SDO AIA 171 starting at 2025-04-11T22:12Z. This field line movement then disturbs surrounding field lines along the southern limb, as seen in GOES SUVI 284. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement using source location seen in UV imagery and several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and a few frames of C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.

note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and the north of STEREO A COR2. The potential source is activity from the vicinity of ARs 4055 (approx. N06W52) and 4058 (approx. N15W53) characterized by brightening best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting at 2025-04-11T23:13Z and opening/moving field lines best seen in SDO AIA 171/193. The eruption is not seen in STEREO A EUV imagery due to a data gap.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as source location. The CME appears to speed up in later frames. The CME may deflect to the east of the potential source location.

note: CME first visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-12T03:24Z. Also visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. A far-sided source is supported by triangulation from SWPC_CAT measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-12T06:36Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. A far-sided source is supported by triangulation from SWPC_CAT measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: Narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source may be an eruption on or near the east limb in SDO AIA 171/193 as moving field lines around 2025-04-12T07:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 (very faint in white light imagery) and STEREO A COR2. This CME is overtaken by the faster CME: 2025-04-12T10:48Z. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. There is some very faint field line movement from beyond the WSW limb best visible in GOES SUVI 284 that could be related. A far-sided source is supported by triangulation from SWPC_CAT measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-04-12T10:48Z. Also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is likely far-sided as there are not any good source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. There is some faint field line movement from beyond the WSW limb starting around 2025-04-12T10:24Z best seen in GOES SUVI 284 that could be related to the source of this CME. cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the faint fuzzy front in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by the likely source location (eruption in a minor unnumbered region).

A wide area of dimming is also visible in SDO AIA 193 and 211, along with field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This event is too faint to be reliably tracked in SOHO LASCO C3.

The same eruption is visible in STEREO A EUVI imagery just to the SW of center disk. This would explain why the CME is not visible in COR2A (it is mostly nose on from the perspective of STEREO A and quite narrow).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on visible source location.

The source is most likely an eruption that is visible near the W limb from the perspective of STEREO A. The eruption is seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 beginning around 2025-05-30T09:35Z near the W limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and on visible source location in STEREO A EUVI.

These features can be seen clearly in SDO AIA 211. This CME overlaps with earlier CME: 2025-05-30T06:38Z which is associated with the M3.4 flare, where as this event is more associated with the subsequent dimming following the flare.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This event is not measurable in SOHO LASCO C3 as it is obscured by the pylon.

A significant area of opening field lines and dimming can be seen from near AR 14100 (N12E12) in SDO AIA 193/171/131/304 and GOES SUVI 284/304 beginning at 2025-05-30T23:47Z, immediately after the flare. Dimming and field line movement extends along a nearby filament which spans across most of the Earth-facing disk, stretching from approximately N30E05 to S15W35, snaking through the entire NW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk in a shape resembling the number '3'. It appears that most of the filamentary material ejected is from the upper lobe of the '3', and departs from approximately N10W15.

note: Jet like CME first seen in the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-31T03:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR in later frames. This eruption can be seen in SDO AIA and STEREO A EUVI 304, along with brightening seen in SDO AIA 94, 131 and field line movement in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This CME is too faint to be reliably measured in SOHO LASCO C3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2. This CME was not visible to measure in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit in STEREO A COR2 and low confidence fit in GOES CCOR. This CME does not reliably appear in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using multiple frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and two usable frames of STEREO A COR2. note: A slow CME to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2, seen more brightly in COR2A and appearing as a faint partial halo in CCOR-1. note: Narrow very faint CME with a fuzzy front seen to the northeast in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs and obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit of the fuzzy faint front in two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2).

This eruption is preceded by a slower outflow of material which was similar in appearance, though more diffuse, and sourced from at or near the same location near the southern limb of the Earth-facing disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. Analysis of this CME was affected by a campaign in STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 as well as visible source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on low confidence triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

The footpoints of the filament are located at approximately AR 14111 (N16W68) and AR 14116 (S10W47).

cmeAnalyses.note: High uncertainty single spacecraft measurement based on imagery from SOHO LASCO C3 and visible source location. Two frames from STEREO A COR2 aided with fit parameters, but the imagery quality was too grainy to be included in the measurement.

note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely an eruption of dimming and a short-lived post eruptive arcade centered around N10E45 starting around 2025-06-20T06:51Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, front is notably faint and difficult to track.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft measurement based on visible deflection in source signature.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2. STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit and possible source location.

note: CME observed as a faint partial halo, nearly a full halo, directed towards the NW in SOHO LASCO C2, and a brighter front to the NE in STEREO A COR. Also faintly observed in currently available frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is a C4.0 flare from AR 14126 (N07W22) which peaked at 2025-06-28T19:54Z observed in SDO AIA 131, alongside brightening in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and a small dimming SW of the region best seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation with SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery only, as they best observe the faint front with available imagery.

note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in SOHO LASCO C3 or STEREO A COR2 despite available imagery. No source for this CME is observed in SDO AIA or GOES SUVI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement with only 3 available frames of SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. CME is deflected northward, thus tracking the front with the swpc_cat tool is difficult.

note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery, and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The potential source is a filament eruption on the NW limb as seen in GOES SUVI 304, with gradual filament liftoff starting around approximately 2025-06-29T10:45Z. Opening field lines also seen in SDO AIA 171/193. Eruption also visible in STEREO A EUVI 195/304. Additional outflowing material may follow this filament eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT. CME not measured in SOHO LASCO C3 because it is obscured by the pylon.

note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery. Not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1. The source is not very clear, but may possibly be a small eruption from AR 14124 (S15E31), best seen as brightening in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284 that deflected to the NE. The eruption starts at 2025-06-29T11:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT, with potential deflection from the source location.

note: Wide bright CME seen to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2A, as well as in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Its source is a prominent eruption of a long filament off the southwest limb seen in SDO AIA 304/193/171 imagery, as well as in EUVI A 195/304 imagery. The filament appears to be potentially wrapping around the limb in both SOHO and STEREO A instruments, so it is hard to estimate the center of this erupting filament. It looks like the filament breaks up in two parts, one seen almost off the west limb in EUVI A 304, and the other part likely having a lower longitude.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis mostly based on the fit with three coronagraphs, but also taking into account that the filament is likely erupting from behind the west limb as seen in SDO AIA.

note: A bright CME seen to the west in all three coronagraphs, which closely follows the 2025-06-29T15:36Z CME and is significantly narrower than this preceding CME. Its source could possibly be the more eastern part of the same filament that produced the 2025-06-29T15:36Z CME, as we see the filament breaking into two parts (this is best seen in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery).

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the fit with three coronagraphs. The source is not very clear.

note: Bright slow lightbulb CME seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 and partially obscured by the pylon in C3. Its source is a slowly developing high northern latitude filament eruption, best seen as a giant loop centered around ~N35W50 (as seen from Stereo A) in EUVI A 304; its clearest view is at 2025-06-29T18:15Z (but it starts lifting off much earlier).

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis based on the location of the erupting filament (N35W90), as seen from STEREO A and on the fit with all three coronagraphs.

note: A very faint CME with a faint fuzzy front to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 and mostly obscured by the pylon in C3, partially overlapping with the slower but brighter 2025-06-29T18:36Z CME. The front of this faint more northern CME is very difficult to trace because of its faintness in any coronagraph other than SOHO. No clear source was found for it, but it might also be connected with the prominent loop-like eruption of the northwestern filament that is happening on/behind the NW limb and which likely produced 2025-06-29T18:36Z CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: An extremely approximate analysis based on the fit of the very faint, difficult to trace front in all three coronagraphs. The source is unclear.

note: This CME is faint but visible to the east/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is too faint to be observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around this time.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

note: This CME is visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. It is not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source location is unknown, but may be related to an eruption near Active Region 14122 (N13W05) starting around 2025-06-30T09:15Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made with STEREO A COR2 imagery using a longitude of -50 degrees due to the unknown source location. Additionally, this event is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery so a triangulated measurement was therefore unavailable.

note: Loop CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. One candidate source is the possible partial eruption of a long filament seen in the SW quadrant of the STEREO-A-facing disk. The long filament is seen starting to move at about 2025-06-30T13:45Z with possible partial liftoff of a portion centered at about S20W130 (heliographic coordinates) seen between the STEREO A EUVI 304 frames timestamped 2025-06-30T15:15-15:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is affected by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 from 2025-06-30T17:06Z-19:06Z caused by a scheduled calibration in SOHO LASCO.

note: Narrow CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is uncertain, but may possibly be subtle field line movement seen from on or beyond the SW limb, at an apparent latitude of about S25, starting around 2025-06-30T17:09Z in SDO AIA 171.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The leading edge becomes diffuse about halfway through the SOHO LASOC C3 field of view.

note: Narrow CME seen to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is uncertain, but opening field lines may possibly be seen on or beyond the North limb in STEREO A EUVI when toggling between frames with timestamp 2025-06-30T18:55Z and 19:05Z in STEREO A EUVI 193. These opening field lines may also seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 between frames 2025-06-30T17:45Z and 19:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Partially obstructed by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1.

note: Faint outflow like CME first seen in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2025-06-30T19:53Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap beginning at 2025-06-30T20:24Z. There was no clear source seen for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

note: Narrow CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 (blocked by pylon in C3), STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is uncertain; there is no clear source in available UV imagery of the disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: Best fit measurement using several frames of STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
